contribs.purpose: Obtain documented compliance clearance for every trade placed for a client account or a staff personal account, so that trades comply with sanctions, restricted-list and client funding rules.
contribs.trigger: Client instructs the RM/ARM to place a trade. / (Compliance-side trigger differs: receipt of the ARM's approval request.)
contribs.inputs: Client trade instruction; trade details (product, notional, direction, client account); client account funding position; agreed product following RM review.
contribs.output: Documented compliance approval or rejection - obtained before placement (pre-trade) or recorded immediately after (post-trade).
contribs.handoff: Approval outcome passed to trade placement (WF-TRADE-001). Approval email retained as the compliance record.
contribs.frequency: Every trade, client accounts and staff personal accounts. Daily / ad hoc. / A large share of trades are placed after 17:00 SGT on US and European markets and therefore follow the post-trade route. / Volume not baselined.
contribs.procedure: Two mutually exclusive paths: pre-trade (office hours) and post-trade (after hours).
contribs.systems: Steps 3, 4, 7, 10: email - free format, no template and no form. / Compliance-side checking systems NOT confirmed. Factiva Dow Jones is used for onboarding KYC; the tool or list used for trade screening is unconfirmed. / No request tracker, no queue, no status visibility.
contribs.data: Product / instrument name, ISIN or product identifier, notional amount, direction, client account number, intended execution bank or venue, client account funding position, staff name where a personal-account trade.
contribs.documents: Approval request email (free format); Compliance approval or rejection email; internal and global white list and black list of stocks; sanctions list. / No standard form or template exists.
contribs.controls: Step 4 / 8 - Compliance checks: / (a) client account funding sufficiency; / (b) internal and global white list and black list of stocks; / (c) sanctioned investments - Russia named, plus drugs and other prohibited companies. / Step 5 - written email approval is the control record; only on 'proceed' may the trade be placed. / General rule: every trade requires a compliance check, before or after. Compliance must be notified either way.
contribs.exceptions: On the post-trade route the trade is already executed when the checks run, so the control is detective rather than preventive. / Step 9: a blacklisted instrument found post-trade must be unwound (bought then sold) and becomes a compliance case. / Step 10: approvals sought and never executed - the client changes their mind or timing moves. Occurs often. / Step 10: a change to the approved package requires fresh approval. / Free-format requests risk omitting information Compliance needs, causing rework. / Whether Compliance can actually block a trade is unconfirmed.
contribs.pain: No template or form - every ARM composes the request differently. / No formal onboarding or training for ARMs; the minimum information Compliance needs is tribal knowledge learned by doing. / Repeated pre-trade approvals for trades that never happen - described in session as a waste of Compliance and ARM time. Frequency unmeasured. / The post-trade route weakens the control while costing the same administrative effort. / Entirely email-based: no status tracking, no queue, no turnaround visibility, no audit-ready record beyond the mailbox.
contribs.kpis: No baseline captured. Needed: / - trades per day / month, split pre-trade vs post-trade / - Compliance turnaround time on approval requests / - percentage of approvals never executed / - number of post-trade breaches and unwinds per period / - rework rate caused by incomplete requests
contribs.source: Interview with Pauline and Jackson, recorded session. / NOT validated with Compliance or with an ARM.

Email the trade details to Compliance requesting approval to execute

On receipt of the 'proceed' confirmation, place the trade

The next morning, or immediately after execution, submit the post-trade approval to Compliance

Where an approved trade is not executed, inform Compliance with the reason -> Compliance / Where the approved package changes (e.g. approved A, B, C but now A, B, D), seek fresh approval

contribs.trigger: RM passes the new client details and onboarding instructions to the ARM.
contribs.inputs: Client particulars from the RM; client KYC documents; Compliance onboarding checklist and guideline; bank-specific account-opening forms.
contribs.output: Complete onboarding pack submitted to Compliance and, on clearance, the confirmed account number received from the bank.
contribs.handoff: ARM informs the RM that the account is open and provides the account number, so the RM can proceed with the client on trading.
contribs.frequency: Ad hoc, driven by RM client acquisition. / Cycle time: roughly 1 month Azimut side, then a further 1 to 1.5 months bank side - a few months in total. Concurrent onboarding volume extends this. / Volume not baselined.
contribs.systems: Email throughout - all sharing and all confirmations. Phone calls for clarification only. / Compliance onboarding checklist and guideline (printed out in practice). / Bank-specific account-opening forms. / NOTE: Compliance's Excel account-opening status tracker is NOT accessible to ARMs - it contains criminal screening information.
contribs.data: Client particulars; identification documents; corporate documents where the client is a corporation (P&L, financial statements); source-of-wealth information; selected service type (advisory / discretionary); target bank; resulting main account and sub-account numbers.
contribs.documents: Compliance onboarding guideline and checklist - the same for all ARMs (copy to be obtained). / Client KYC documents. / Bank account-opening forms, specific to each bank. / Compliance clearance email; bank account-opening confirmation email.
contribs.controls: Step 3 - ARM completeness check against the Compliance checklist before submission; every item must be ticked. / Sequencing control: Azimut's screening must clear before the pack goes to the bank. Not parallel - when Azimut submits, it is Azimut's responsibility that the client is clean. / Single point of contact: the bank never contacts the client directly; all contact runs through Compliance or the ARM. / Email is the evidence record - face-to-face is described as the riskiest channel because it cannot be evidenced.
contribs.exceptions: Compliance returns the request for more client information where screening raises a repeated prompt or risk indicator. / The bank may go deeper or request further supporting documents - more common for corporations. It contacts Compliance or the ARM. / Where Compliance cannot answer the bank's query it passes back to the ARM. / Where the bank raises something serious (e.g. a crime issue) and cannot onboard, it escalates to the RM and management. / Frequency of this back-and-forth is unknown - to be confirmed.
contribs.pain: Document verification is the bottleneck, not screening - screening itself takes about 5 minutes once the name is entered; verifying whether submitted documents are genuine and sufficient is what consumes the time. / Preparing the account-opening forms is slow and manual, and forms differ per bank. / Documents are largely hard copy - Compliance is described as working from a stack of paper. / The ARM cannot see onboarding status because the tracker is Compliance-only, so progress must be chased by email. / Total elapsed time of a few months sits against a market expectation of far less.
contribs.kpis: No baseline captured. Needed: / - accounts opened per month, and concurrent open cases / - elapsed time from RM handover to Compliance submission / - Compliance clearance time; bank clearance time / - number of information requests per case (Compliance-side and bank-side) / - first-time-right rate on submitted packs
contribs.source: Interview with Pauline and Jackson, recorded session. / NOT validated with Compliance or with an ARM.

contribs.trigger: ARM receives the split retrocession report for their RMs from Finance by email.
contribs.inputs: Split bank retrocession report; trade blotter (shared Google Sheet); RM confirmation.
contribs.output: Validated retrocession amount, agreed with the RM.
contribs.handoff: ARM emails the confirmed amounts, listed by RM, to Operations Finance.
contribs.frequency: Quarterly, per bank. Reports arrive 1 to 1.5 months after quarter end and everything must close by roughly month 1.5 because commission calculation follows immediately. / One ARM typically serves 2-3 RMs; approximately 12 ARMs across 6 teams. / Unit of measure agreed: number of trade line items, NOT notional amount.
contribs.systems: Trade blotter - a shared Google Sheet, one worksheet per RM, shared between the ARM and Operations Finance. A Portfolio Management System (external vendor) is being implemented to replace it. / Email to Finance and to the bank. Email or WhatsApp to the RM, by each pair's own arrangement. / Excel for any working.
contribs.data: From the blotter: bank, notional amount traded, value date, settlement date, product placed, estimated fee expected per trade. / From the bank report: reported retrocession fee per transaction, client account number, ISIN or transaction number. / Output: confirmed allocation per RM.
contribs.documents: Split bank retrocession report (Excel or PDF - format differs by bank). / Trade blotter. / Confirmation email to Finance. / Bank clarification correspondence.
contribs.controls: Step 4 - line-by-line comparison against the trade blotter. The blotter is the source of truth. / Step 6 - RM approval required before confirming to Finance; the final call is always the RM's. / Step 8 - the reply must state the item name and the confirmed amount. 'OK, proceed' is not acceptable because Finance has no amount to record. / The ARM is always the party liaising with Finance; Finance does not deal directly with RMs.
contribs.exceptions: Bank pays less than the blotter estimate. / Trade placed but absent from the bank's report ('incomplete fees') - resolved by going back to the counterparty with trade date, settlement value, product, notional and expected fee. / Blotter not maintained at the point of trade, leaving no baseline for the comparison. / Clarification with the bank sits with the ARM unless the RM chooses to handle it.
contribs.pain: Manual line-by-line comparison against a spreadsheet. / The estimated fee in the blotter is a rough figure, so discrepancies require judgement rather than a clean match. / No standard reply format - each ARM composes their own, which pushes consolidation effort onto Finance. / Where an ARM serves several RMs they repeat the split downwards themselves. / Blotter data is manually keyed and described as prone to error.
contribs.kpis: No baseline captured. Needed: line items checked per cycle; discrepancy rate; number and turnaround of bank clarifications; ARM hours per cycle; cycle time from report receipt to confirmation.
contribs.source: Interview with Pauline and Jackson, recorded session. / NOT validated with an ARM.

contribs.controls: Step 4 - line-by-line comparison against the trade blotter. / Step 6 - RM approval required before confirming to Finance. / Step 8 - reply must state item name and confirmed amount. / ARM is the sole liaison with Finance.

contribs.kpis: No baseline captured. Needed: line items checked per cycle; number of counterparties reporting by email vs Excel; discrepancy rate; ARM hours per monthly cycle.
contribs.source: Interview with Pauline. Described as structurally identical to retrocession. / Not validated with an ARM. The ARM-side detail is inferred from the retrocession walkthrough, which the session confirmed as 'the same process'.

contribs.purpose: Bill the client the management fee and performance fee due for direct management services, in accordance with the signed client fee letter.
contribs.trigger: The client fee letter, which defines the billing frequency. Billing then runs on that periodic cycle.
contribs.inputs: Client fee letter (account number, management fee %, performance fee %, calculation method, charging period, high water mark terms); portfolio NAV or AUM for the period.
contribs.output: Fee calculation and supporting appendix, approved by the RM and converted into an official tax invoice by Finance.
contribs.handoff: ARM sends the tax invoice to the client, or to the bank for auto-debit, per the client's payment arrangement.
contribs.frequency: Set by each client's fee letter - quarterly, semi-annual or annual. NOT uniformly quarterly. / Volume not baselined.
contribs.systems: ARM's own Excel - the calculation is built in the ARM's own spreadsheet, not a shared model. / Email to the RM, to Finance, to the client and to the bank. / Finance raises the invoice in Xero (Finance column).
contribs.data: Client account number; management fee percentage; performance fee percentage; calculation method (typically NAV or AUM x fee); charging period; high water mark position; period NAV or AUM; calculated fee amount.
contribs.documents: Client fee letter - drafted by Legal on a standard template, signed by the client at onboarding, and also sent by Legal to Finance so Finance can verify calculations. / Fee calculation and supporting appendix, prepared by the ARM. / Official tax invoice, created by Finance in Xero.
contribs.controls: Three-stage control: ARM prepares -> RM reviews -> Finance provides a second pair of eyes before the invoice is raised. / Step 3 - RM must communicate the fee to the client and clear it before the invoice request is raised. / Step 5 - Finance verifies the period, amounts and formulas against the fee letter. Finance does NOT redo the calculation. / The fee letter is the governing document for every check.
contribs.exceptions: Finance rejects where the calculation does not match the fee letter. Examples given: the fee letter says 0.8% but the calculation uses 0.5%; or the fee is effective from June but the calculation starts from May. / Both arise because the calculation is done in the ARM's own Excel. / High water mark errors - performance fee charged on a gain below the established high water mark. / Client disputes the fee at step 3, requiring recalculation.
contribs.pain: The calculation lives in each ARM's own Excel, so there is no shared, version-controlled model and no way to enforce the fee letter terms in the calculation itself. / Errors are caught late - at the Finance check, after the RM has already reviewed and in some cases after the client has been told. / High water mark tracking is manual and depends on the ARM knowing the prior peak. / Frequency varies per client, so there is no single billing run - each client's cycle must be tracked separately.
contribs.kpis: No baseline captured. Needed: invoices raised per cycle; Finance rejection rate and reasons; time from fee letter trigger to invoice issued; number of clients per billing frequency; days sales outstanding on client fees.
contribs.source: Interview with Pauline and Jackson. Purpose and trigger corrected in session - the trigger is the fee letter, not quarter end. / Not validated with an ARM.
